title: Hosted API - Embeddings & Rerank demo (NovusFind)
summary: Intro/demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking pipeline for search relevance. Covered embedding models, batch vs streaming, prefix/K V cache, rerank endpoint, tradeoffs (latency vs cost), security questions (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and next steps: run a small pilot, share pricing and security pack, benchmark with 50k queries.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Samir from Redwood inference, and with me is Jane our solutions engineer...sorry carlos is on as well. How's every one doing?
[00:18] Emily: good thanks, excited to see how you might help our search relevance problems.
[00:24] Samir: Great — quick agenda, we will do a 20 minute demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, show console, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:37] Jane: I'll start with the embeddings flow, so at a high level we take your docs, run them through our embeddings endpoint, store vectors, and then at query time we do a nearest neighbor search and optionally call our rerank endpoint which runs a cross-encoder style model to rescore top N.
[01:05] Ravi: couple of quick context items, our current infra is elasticsearch with faiss for vector store, mostly GCP, and latency SLOs are 200ms p99.
[01:22] Jane: totally. For hosted api we expose both embeddings and rerank endpoints. embeddings are optimized for throughput, batching, and you can choose model family — we have small-medium-large tradeoffs. rerank is a second call that takes candidate ids + query and returns a ranking.
[02:03] Marta: are you doing the rerank on the same GPU as embeddings? curious about cost.
[02:09] Jane: in hosted mode rerank runs on our inference pool; it's a different model and costs more per call. Theres two levers for cost: reduce candidate size like top 10, or use a cheaper cross-encoder model. We also do automatic batching to amortize cost.
[02:35] Samir: one thing customers like is prefix/K V cache to speed up repeated tokens — sorry thats K V cache, sometimes ASR shows K V — it helps for conversational but for rerank it's mostly fresh scoring per request.
[02:50] Emily: can you show the console? we want to see latency and token breakdowns.
[02:55] Jane: yeah, quick screen share — im pulling up the console. (screen share noise)
[03:12] Jane: On the console you can see per-route latency, token-level cost, and the rerank request breakdown. here's an example of a search flow: embeddings store X vectors, query returns top 50 and then rerank for top 10.
[04:05] Ben: What about integration? we use python microservices, node for frontend.
[04:12] Carlos: Our SDKs cover both python and node, plus a simple REST curl example.
[04:20] Jane: I'll show the curl for embeddings and rerank. (typing) curl -X POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-small and then for rerank POST /v1/rerank {query, candidates: [{id, text}], model: redwood-rerank-medium}
[04:50] Ravi: any limits on candidate length or token size?
[04:55] Jane: we have per-request token limits — for embeddings typically 8k tokens, rerank models vary; we can share exact limits in the security pack.
[05:12] Emily: you mentioned batching — does that introduce latency spikes?
[05:18] Jane: we do continuous batching tuned for latency SLOs, so for low traffic we don't wait long; for high throughput we batch to reduce cost. you can configure latency targets per route in Dedicated, hosted has sensible defaults.
[06:00] Marta: security — we need SOC2 type II, SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
[06:10] Samir: we are SOC2 certified, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and can integrate with KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For hosted we offer encryption at rest and detailed audit logs; i'll send the full pack.
[06:32] Emily: data residency — some EU queries must stay in eu-west. do you have region pinning?
[06:37] Carlos: yes, hosted across regions and you can pin routes to regions or use Dedicated/Private for stricter residency.
[06:50] Ben: competitors? we evaluated algolia and openai + pinecone combo.
[06:55] Samir: that's common — we often position vs algolia for relevance features and vs the openai+pinecone pattern for cost/latency.
[07:12] Jane: back to demo — here's a simple notebook where i ingest a small doc set, create embeddings, then run a query.
[07:30] (typing and demo noise)
[08:05] Jane: results come back with a similarity score. then we call rerank — note the rerank api takes the query + full passages for top K and returns a new score and explanation tokens sometimes.
[08:30] Emily: does rerank return explainability? we need to show why results changed.
[08:35] Jane: we return feature level signals and a short rationale field for enterprise models. it's not a full LLM explanation but helpful.
[09:00] Ravi: our p99 is strict — will rerank add 50-100ms?
[09:08] Jane: depends on model size and candidate count. for an optimized medium rerank on our hosted pool, typical extra latency is 30-80ms when reranking top 5. If you rerank top 50 it can climb.
[09:36] Samir: we also have a caching pattern — if the same query appears often you can cache the final rerank result; for prefix heavy apps caching helps.
[09:52] Marta: how do you measure quality? we run A/B tests internally.
[09:58] Jane: yes we recommend a labeled set and run rerank A/B with clickthrough metrics; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant and model configs.
[10:18] Emily: could you do a small benchmark with our dataset? 50k queries over a couple days.
[10:25] Samir: absolutely, we can do a pilot — we'll run hosted benchmark and compare to your current baseline.
[10:35] Ben: pricing question — how do you charge?
[10:39] Samir: hosted charges per-embedding unit and per-rerank call; embeddings per vector and per token for some models, rerank per call. i'll include an example invoice with numbers for topologies.
[11:02] Jane: quick detour — for high throughput Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools and you can pin models to hardware to reduce variance.
[11:20] Ravi: for Dedicated do you support VPC peering and customer-managed kms?
[11:26] Carlos: yes, Dedicated and Private support VPC, SFTP for logs, and bring-your-own-kms options.
[11:42] Emily: what about model versioning and rollouts? we can't risk a bad model breaking search.
[11:49] Jane: we support model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallbacks to previous model variants. you can configure percent-based rollouts in the console.
[12:10] (demo continues; jane runs a query showing console traces)
[13:30] Jane: you can see token-level time series and a per-route cost breakdown — this helps decide between cheaper embed + bigger rerank vs larger embedding model.
[14:05] Marta: is there an option to run embeddings locally and only use your rerank?
[14:12] Samir: yes you can self-host embeddings and call our rerank, that pattern is supported; it's common for customers who want to control vector store.
[14:30] Emily: do you integrate with Pinecone/Weaviate or only provide API?
[14:36] Carlos: we integrate with popular vector stores via connectors; we also have first-class recommendations for faiss/annoy/pgvector.
[15:05] Ben: any SLA for p99 latency?
[15:09] Samir: Hosted has best-effort with historical profiles; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency targets depending on contract.
[15:25] Ravi: we have compliance reviews next tuesday with legal — can you send SOC report and pen test?
[15:31] Samir: yes will share SOC2 type II + pen test and whitepapers.
[15:40] Jane: also sharing a benchmark spreadsheet template so you can drop sample queries and we'll run head to head.
[16:00] (demo wrap-up)
[16:12] Emily: quick note on rerank costs — if we rerank everything that could be expensive. any recommendations?
[16:20] Jane: typical best practice: do ANN top 50 with embeddings, then rerank top 5. use a smaller rerank model for head traffic and larger for tail, or use a throttle on rerank for certain query types.
[16:50] Samir: to recap next steps: 1) we run a 2-week pilot with 50k queries, 2) we send pricing + security pack, 3) schedule a technical deep dive to discuss Dedicated options.
[17:05] Marta: timeline — we are aiming for an initial pilot in november and production by q1.
[17:12] Ben: who will own the pilot on redwood side?
[17:16] Samir: i'll own the engagement, jane will run benchmarks, carlos handles security.
[17:25] Emily: any blockers for us starting the pilot?
[17:29] Samir: a signed pilot MSA and access to a subset of your dataset, plus a contact for ingestion.
[17:45] Ravi: can you provide sample ingest scripts?
[17:49] Jane: yes, the notebook i showed is the sample; i'll share the link.
[18:05] (wrap up chatter, small cross talk)
[18:30] Samir: thanks everyone we'll follow up with an email with attachments.
[38:50] (call ends)
